definitions.explanation: Describes the state of not giving proper attention or care to something that deserves it. Often used to criticize lack of diligence or to express one's commitment to not neglect something.

examples.japanese: {勉強|べんきょう}を{疎|おろそ}かにしてはいけない。
examples.english: You must not neglect your studies.

examples.japanese: {健康管理|けんこうかんり}を{疎|おろそ}かにしがちだ。
examples.english: I tend to neglect health management.

examples.japanese: {基本|きほん}を{疎|おろそ}かにすると{失敗|しっぱい}する。
examples.english: If you neglect the basics, you will fail.

examples.japanese: {家族|かぞく}との{時間|じかん}を{疎|おろそ}かにしていた{自分|じぶん}を{反省|はんせい}した。
examples.english: I reflected on how I had been neglecting time with my family.

notes:
{疎|おろそ}か is typically used with にする (to neglect something) or になる (to become neglected).

Common patterns:
- 〜を{疎|おろそ}かにする (to neglect something)
- 〜が{疎|おろそ}かになる (something becomes neglected)
- {疎|おろそ}かにしがち (tend to neglect)

Note: The kanji {疎|おろそ}か is often written in hiragana (おろそか) in everyday use.

Related words:
- {蔑|ないがしろ}にする: to neglect, disregard (stronger, more deliberate)
- {怠|なま}ける: to be lazy, slack off
- {軽視|けいし}する: to make light of, underestimate
